grammar.text_or_setswana: In Setswana, how you greet and say goodbye depends on how many people you are speaking to.
Talking to one person, use Dumela, O tsogile jang? and O kae?. Talking to two or more people, use Dumelang, Le tsogile jang? and Le kae?.
Address people politely with rra (to one man) or mma (to one woman); for more than one, use borra or bomma.
When you part, the word depends on who is leaving and who is staying: the one staying says Tsamaya sentle ("go well") to the one leaving, and the one leaving says Sala sentle ("stay well") back.
Robala sentle ("sleep well") is used at night instead of Tsamaya sentle or Sala sentle.
Dumela, rra.
grammar.english: Hello, sir.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Dumelang, bomma.
grammar.english: Hello, ladies.

grammar.text_or_setswana: O tsogile jang? Ke tsogile sentle.
grammar.english: How did you wake up? I woke up well.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Le kae? Re teng.
grammar.english: How are you (to several people)? We are fine.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Tsamaya sentle. Sala sentle.
grammar.english: Go well. Stay well.

grammar.text_or_setswana: The start of a verb changes to match who is doing the action: ke (I), o (you, one person), o (she or he), re (we), lo (you, several people), ba (they).
With bua (speak): Ke bua Setswana. O bua Sekgoa. Re bua Setswana. Lo bua eng? Ba bua Setswana.
With tswa (come from): Ke tswa kwa Gaborone. O tswa kae? Re tswa kwa Molepolole.
With nna (be): Ke nna Kabelo. — I am Kabelo. The full pronoun can stand before it: Nna ke nna Kabelo.
To stress or contrast who is acting
grammar.english: put the pronoun first: Nna ke bua Sekgoa. Wena o bua Setswana. Bona ba bua Setswana.

grammar.text_or_setswana: le joins two things: Setswana le Sekgoa (Setswana and English). kwa marks a place: kwa Gaborone (in Gaborone / from Gaborone).
leina (name) is a class 5 noun; its plural is maina. leina la me = my name; leina la gago = your name. mang asks who: Leina la gago ke mang?
Survival phrases for now, explained in later units: Ga ke tlhaloganye (I don't understand), Bua ka bonya tswee-tswee (speak slowly, please), Ke eng ka Setswana? (what is it in Setswana?).
Ke nna Kabelo.
grammar.english: I am Kabelo.

grammar.text_or_setswana: O tswa kae? Ke tswa kwa Francistown.
grammar.english: Where are you from? I come from Francistown.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Leina la me ke Neo. Leina la gago ke mang?
grammar.english: My name is Neo. What is your name?

grammar.text_or_setswana: Nna ke bua Setswana le Sekgoa.
grammar.english: I speak Setswana and English.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Ga ke tlhaloganye. Bua ka bonya tswee-tswee.
grammar.english: I don't understand. Speak slowly, please.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Class 1 nouns for people start with mo-; their class 2 plurals start with ba-: mosadi → basadi. monna → banna. motho → batho.
Some people nouns (classes 1a/2a) just add bo- for the plural: mosetsana → bosetsana. mosimane → bosimane. kgaitsadi → bokgaitsadi.
ngwana → bana is irregular — learn the pair as it is.
To say something belongs to someone, use wa (one person) or ba (people) + the owner: me (me), gago (you), gagwe (him or her).
For one person: ngwana wa me (my child). mosadi wa gagwe (his wife). For people: bana ba me (my children). bana ba gagwe (her children).
Kinship does not use wa/ba — it has its own fused forms: mme (my mother), rre (my father), mmago (your mother), rrago (your father), mmaagwe (his or her mother), rraagwe (his or her father).
Yo ke… points at someone in a picture: Yo ke mmaagwe. (This is his mother.)
Yo ke ngwana wa me.
grammar.english: This is my child.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Bana ba me ke mosetsana le mosimane.
grammar.english: My children are a girl and a boy.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Yo ke mmaagwe.
grammar.english: This is his mother.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Mosadi yo ke kgaitsadi wa me.
grammar.english: This woman is my sister.

grammar.text_or_setswana: To say you do NOT do something, use ga ke + the verb with its final -a changed to -e: Ke batla (I want) → Ga ke batle (I don't want).
With we or they the same: ga re, ga ba + -e. Re nwa metsi (we drink water) → Ga re nwe metsi (we don't drink water).
ja (eat) is irregular: Ga ke je nama (I don't eat meat) — not ga ke ja. nwa (drink) follows the rule: Ga ke nwe.
Ke lapile = I'm hungry. Ke kuneng = I'm full. kgotsa = or: Tee kgotsa kofi? (tea or coffee?)
Patterns for now, not tested: Ke a ja (I am eating) vs Ke ja nama (I eat meat); yes/no questions with A o …? (A o batla metsi? — do you want water?); Ke batla go ja (I want to eat).
Ke batla nama. Ga ke batle borotho.
grammar.english: I want meat. I don't want bread.

grammar.text_or_setswana: O batla eng? Ke kopa metsi tswee-tswee.
grammar.english: What do you want? I'd like water, please.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Ga ke nwe tee. Ke nwa kofi.
grammar.english: I don't drink tea. I drink coffee.

grammar.text_or_setswana: A o ja nama? Nnyaa ga ke je nama.
grammar.english: Do you eat meat? No, I don't eat meat.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Re batla bogobe le morogo.
grammar.english: We want porridge and greens.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Counting: nngwe (1). pedi (2). tharo (3). nne (4). tlhano (5). tshela (6). supa (7). robedi (8). robongwe (9). shome (10).
Eleven is lesome le nngwe — ten and one. The tens are masome a + the class 6 form: masome a mabedi (20). masome a mararo (30). masome a mane (40). masome a matlhano (50) … up to lekgolo (100).
To say how many of a class 10 noun, use noun + di le + number: dipula di le pedi (two pula). dingwaga di le nne (four years).
Ke bokae? asks the price: Ke bokae? (How much is it?)
Age: O na le dingwaga di le kae? (How old are you?) Ke na le dingwaga di le tlhano. (I am five years old.)
thata = a lot. tsotlhe = all. nngwe fela = only one.
Ke bokae? Dipula di le tlhano.
grammar.english: How much is it? Five pula.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Dipula di le pedi.
grammar.english: Two pula.

grammar.text_or_setswana: O na le dingwaga di le kae? Ke na le dingwaga di le robedi.
grammar.english: How old are you? I am eight years old.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Ke reka lerotse le apole.
grammar.english: I am buying a sweet melon and an apple.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Some nouns start with se-; their plurals start with di-: sejana → dijana. setilo → ditilo. senotlolo → dinotlolo. selo → dilo.
Some nouns start with le-; their plurals start with ma-: lebati → mabati. lebone → mabone. lentswe → mantswe. lejwe → majwe.
You already know pairs like this: setshwantsho → ditshwantsho, leina → maina, lelapa → malapa, leselo → maselo, and mosadi → basadi (mo-/ba-).
Irregular pairs to learn as they are: ntlo → matlo (house). lee → mae (egg).
Ke eng? asks what something is. Answer with Ke + the name: Ke eng? — Ke setilo. (What is it? It is a chair.)
Ke eng? Ke sejana.
grammar.english: What is it? It is a cup.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Ke eng? Ke buka le pena.
grammar.english: What is it? It is a book and a pen.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Ke eng? Ga ke itse.
grammar.english: What is it? I don't know.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Bula lebati. Tswala lebati.
grammar.english: Open the door. Close the door.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Bala buka. Kwala leina la gago.
grammar.english: Read a book. Write your name.

grammar.text_or_setswana: To say where something is, put kwa or mo before the place and add -ng to it: kwa toropong (in town). mo ntlung (in the house). kwa sekolong (at school). mo tulong (on the seat).

The ending changes: words ending in -a take -eng (tsela → tseleng, noka → nokeng); words ending in -o take -u + -ng (ntlo → ntlung). Exceptions: gae takes no kwa change (kwa gae, ke ya gae) and place names take no -ng (kwa Gaborone).
Near and far: gaufi (near), kgakala (far). A go gaufi? (Is it near?) A go kgakala? (Is it far?)
To find a place, don't ask a where-question with the noun — say Ke batla… (I'm looking for…) or Botsa tsela (ask for the way).
O dula kae? asks where someone lives. Answer: Ke dula kwa toropong. (I live in town.)
Ke batla lebentlele. A go gaufi?
grammar.english: I'm looking for a shop. Is it near?

grammar.text_or_setswana: Ke dula kwa toropong.
grammar.english: I live in town.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Nnyaa go kgakala. Tsamaya ka bese.
grammar.english: No, it's far. Go by bus.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Ke ya kwa sekolong.
grammar.english: I am going to school.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Ke ya gae.
grammar.english: I am going home.

grammar.text_or_setswana: The days: Mosupologo (Monday). Labobedi (Tuesday). Laboraro (Wednesday). Labone (Thursday). Labotlhano (Friday). Matlhatso (Saturday). Tshipi (Sunday).
Use ka + the time word: ka Labobedi (on Tuesday). ka mosogare (in the morning). ka maitseboa (in the evening). ka bosego (at night).
Clock time is whole hours only: ka ura ya nne (at four o'clock). maabane (yesterday). moso (tomorrow). jaanong (now).
O tsoga ka ura efe? (What time do you wake up?) Ke tsoga ka ura ya robedi. (I wake up at eight.)
Ka Labobedi ke bereka.
grammar.english: On Tuesday I work.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Ke nwa tee ka mosogare.
grammar.english: I drink tea in the morning.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Ka Tshipi ga ke bereke.
grammar.english: On Sunday I don't work.

grammar.text_or_setswana: Jaanong ke a ja.
grammar.english: Now I am eating.

questions.prompt: You greet a group of three friends. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Dumelang is used for two or more people; Dumela is for one person.

questions.prompt: You are leaving and your friend is staying. What do you say to them?
questions.explanation: The one who leaves says Sala sentle ("stay well") to the one staying.

questions.prompt: How do you politely address one man (word for "sir")?
questions.explanation: rra addresses one man; borra addresses several men.

questions.prompt: Someone asks you "Le kae?" Who are they asking?
questions.explanation: Le kae? is the plural form of O kae?, asked to more than one person.

questions.prompt: Fill in: you are staying and your friend is leaving. You say "___ sentle."
questions.explanation: The one who stays says Tsamaya sentle ("go well") to the one leaving.

questions.prompt: You greet two ladies in the morning. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Two people = Dumelang; ladies = bomma.

questions.prompt: It is bedtime. What do you say to someone going to sleep?
questions.explanation: Robala sentle is the goodnight farewell.

questions.prompt: What phrase means "thank you"?
questions.explanation: Ke a leboga is the standard way to say thank you.

questions.prompt: How do you reply when someone asks "O tsogile jang?"
questions.explanation: Ke tsogile sentle is the standard reply, meaning "I woke up well."

questions.prompt: Two men greet you. How should you greet them back?
questions.explanation: Two men = borra (plural of rra); more than one person = Dumelang.

questions.prompt: In the dialogue, who greets first?
questions.explanation: Rra Molefe opens with "Dumela, mma."

questions.prompt: How does Mma Kagiso say she woke up?
questions.explanation: She replies "Ke tsogile sentle" — I woke up well.

questions.prompt: How does Rra Molefe say he is feeling?
questions.explanation: Rra Molefe replies "Ke teng, ke a leboga" — I'm fine, thank you.

questions.prompt: Who says "Sala sentle" at the end, and why?
questions.answer: Rra Molefe, because he is leaving
questions.distractors: Mma Kagiso, because she is leaving|Rra Molefe, because Mma Kagiso is leaving|Mma Kagiso, because Rra Molefe is leaving
questions.explanation: Mma Kagiso stays and says Tsamaya sentle to Rra Molefe; he is leaving, so he replies Sala sentle.

questions.prompt: Which start do you put on a verb to say "I"?
questions.explanation: Ke is the subject concord for I: Ke bua (I speak).

questions.prompt: How do you say They speak Setswana.?
questions.distractors: Re bua Setswana|Ke bua Setswana|Lo bua Setswana
questions.explanation: Ba is the concord for they (bone): Ba bua Setswana.

questions.prompt: Fill in: ___ bua Sekgoa. (we)
questions.explanation: Re is the concord for we (rona): Re bua Sekgoa.

questions.prompt: You ask one person where they are from. What do you say?
questions.distractors: Le tswa kae?|Ke tswa kae?|Ba tswa kae?
questions.explanation: O is the concord for you (one person): O tswa kae?

questions.prompt: Fill in: Ke nna Kabelo. ___ nna Neo. (you, one person)
questions.explanation: O is the concord for you (one person): O nna Neo.

questions.prompt: Which pronoun stresses "they" at the start of a sentence?
questions.explanation: bone is the emphatic form of they: Bona ba bua Setswana.

questions.prompt: What does "Leina la me ke Neo." mean?
questions.distractors: Your name is Neo.|His name is Neo.|What is your name?
questions.explanation: Leina la me ke… = my name is…

questions.prompt: Someone says "Ga ke tlhaloganye." What do they mean?
questions.distractors: I don't know you|I am not from here|I don't speak slowly
questions.explanation: Ga ke tlhaloganye = I don't understand.

questions.prompt: You forgot a Setswana word. How do you ask what it is in Setswana?
questions.explanation: Ke eng ka Setswana? asks for the Setswana word.

questions.prompt: Fill in: Ke bua Sekgoa ___. (only English)
questions.explanation: fela means only and follows the word it limits: Sekgoa fela.

questions.prompt: How do you say We come from Gaborone.?
questions.distractors: Ke tswa kwa Gaborone|Ba tswa kwa Gaborone|O tswa kwa Gaborone
questions.explanation: Re is the concord for we: Re tswa kwa Gaborone.

questions.prompt: You greet two people and ask where they are from. What do you say?
questions.distractors: O tswa kae?|Ke tswa kae?|Ba tswa kae?
questions.explanation: Two or more people take the concord lo: Le tswa kae?

questions.prompt: Fill in: ___ ke bua Sekgoa. Wena o bua Setswana. (as for me)
questions.explanation: Nna stresses I in contrast with wena (you).

questions.prompt: What does "O bua eng?" ask about?
questions.distractors: Where you are from|What your name is|Who you are
questions.explanation: eng = what; O bua eng? = what do you speak / say?

questions.prompt: Write in Setswana: "My name is Neo."
questions.explanation: Leina la me ke… = my name is…

questions.prompt: Someone asks you Leina la gago ke mang? What is a good answer?
questions.distractors: Ke tswa kwa Gaborone|Ee|Ga ke tlhaloganye
